stateOfPlay: Eisenkot's Yashar leads Likud 23 to 20, and both blocs have slipped: the Netanyahu bloc sits at 52, the change bloc at 51. Neither is close on its own. The change bloc plus Ra'am reaches only 57 — the arithmetic now works exactly once, if Yoaz Hendel's Reservists join too, and that lands on 61 with nothing to spare. Ra'am has made itself easier to sit with: Yoav Segelovich, formerly of Yesh Atid, has joined its list. Hendel is the harder problem — he has ruled out Shas and UTJ over the draft, and has been cool on relying on Ra'am. On the right, Ofer Winter's Amcha Yisrael takes four seats and says it will recommend Netanyahu, splitting the vote Netanyahu warned it would.
raamNote: Ra'am is no longer the untouchable partner it was. Yoav Segelovich — a former Yesh Atid MK and deputy internal security minister — now runs on its list, the first Jewish figure to do so. That is aimed squarely at the Zionist opposition's objection to relying on it, and it is the reason a change-bloc government is arithmetically thinkable at all.
